classification.difficultyReason: Select SSS, RHS and SAS from explicitly scaffolded givens, then use matching angles/sides and the straight angle to derive each theorem without circular use.

content.prompt: This question leads you through the proofs of the three theorems in the text about the midpoint of a chord.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Prove that: The line joining the midpoint of a chord to the centre is perpendicular to the chord, and bisects the angle at the centre subtended by the chord.

Let M be the midpoint of the chord AB.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, lower chord AB and midpoint M. Segments OA, OB and OM are drawn. Matching double ticks mark AM and MB. O is marked with a red dot.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: AO=BO (radii), AM=BM (midpoint), and OM is common. Therefore $\triangle AOM\equiv\triangle BOM$ (SSS).

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence, prove that OM ⟂ AB and that OM bisects ∠AOB.

answer.short: OM is perpendicular to AB and bisects the angle AOB.
answer.worked: The matching angles AMO and BMO are equal and sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$ and $OM\perp AB$. Matching angles AOM and BOM are equal, so OM bisects $\angle AOB$.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Prove that: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord, and bisects the angle at the centre subtended by the chord.

Let M be the foot of the perpendicular from O to chord AB.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, lower chord AB, segments OA and OB, and perpendicular OM meeting AB at M. A right-angle square is supplied between MO and MB. O is marked with a red dot.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Both triangles are right-angled at M; AO=BO (radii) and OM is common. Thus $\triangle AOM\equiv\triangle BOM$ (RHS).

children.label: iv
children.prompt: Hence, prove that M is the midpoint of AB and that OM bisects ∠AOB.

answer.short: M is the midpoint of AB and OM bisects the angle AOB.
answer.worked: Matching sides give AM=BM, so M is the midpoint of AB. Matching angles give $\angle AOM=\angle BOM$, so OM bisects $\angle AOB$.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Prove that: The bisector of the angle at the centre subtended by a chord bisects the chord, and is perpendicular to it.

Let the bisector of $\angle AOB$ meet the chord AB at M.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, lower chord AB, segments OA, OB and OM. M lies on AB. Both ∠AOM and ∠MOB are labelled α. O is marked with a red dot.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: AO=BO (radii), $\angle AOM=\angle BOM$ (bisector), and OM is common. Hence $\triangle AOM\equiv\triangle BOM$ (SAS).

children.label: vi
children.prompt: Hence, prove that M is the midpoint of AB and that OM ⟂ AB.

answer.short: M is the midpoint of AB and OM is perpendicular to AB.
answer.worked: Matching sides give AM=BM, so M is the midpoint. Matching angles AMO and BMO are equal and sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$ and $OM\perp AB$.
